post.description:
Creates a new user account or authenticates existing user using SSO provider authorization.
  Supports automatic account linking and guest session merging.
  
  Flow:
  1. Client obtains authorization code from SSO provider
  2. Client sends code and redirect URI
  3. Server exchanges code for SSO provider tokens
  4. Server checks if user with SSO email exists:
      - If exists: Links SSO provider to account (if not linked)
      - If new: Creates account with SSO profile data
  5. Merges any existing guest session data if JWT provided
  
  Account Handling:
  - For existing users: Links new SSO provider if not already linked
  - For new users: Creates account with verified email
  - Profile information is populated from SSO provider
  - SSO connection is established for future logins
  
  Session Merging:
  - If a guest JWT token is provided, all associated resources are transferred
  - Merged resources include: preferences, saved items etc.
  - Guest session is cleaned up after successful merge
  - Original resource IDs and timestamps are preserved
  
  Notes:
  - Seamlessly handles both new and existing users (SUSI pattern)
  - Multiple SSO providers can be linked to single account

post.description:
Handles Facebook data deletion requests as required by Facebook Platform Policy.
  
  When users request to delete their data from Facebook, Facebook sends a signed request
  to this endpoint containing the user's Facebook ID. The system will:
  
  1. Validate the signed request from Facebook
  2. Find the associated user account by Facebook ID or email
  3. Delete the user's account and all associated data
  4. Return a confirmation code and status URL for tracking
  
  This endpoint is called directly by Facebook's systems when users initiate
  data deletion through their Facebook settings.
  
  The signed request contains the user's Facebook ID and is cryptographically
  signed by Facebook using the app secret to ensure authenticity.

    * Magic link verification
  - All associated data is preserved during conversion
  
  Limitations:

  - Session has extended but finite validity
  - Must be converted to retain data long-term

info.title: Mobitrace API
info.description:
Mobitrace backend API — phone number reverse-lookup and identity-protection reports.

  Core Features:
  - Reverse-lookup reports (carrier pre-check, data breach, sex offender, social network sections)
  - Location requests with consent flow
  - Async report generation and PDF export via background jobs
  - Subscription-gated upsellings for paid report content
  - Activity history feed and admin management panel

  Authentication:
  - JWT Bearer token required for authorized endpoints
  - SSO support for seamless integration
  - Okta SSO for admin endpoints

  Data Management:
  - PostgreSQL via Prisma; Redis-backed lookup rate limiting; S3-compatible file storage

  API Access:
  - Public endpoints: /api
  - Yaml version: /api-yaml
  - JSON version: /api-json
  - Documentation: /docs
  - Protected routes require authentication
  - Rate limiting applies to all endpoints

Declared required for the same reason `details` is — both are documented by what the formatter sends, not by whether a caller happens to need them (#112). details.description: Additional context about the error. A validation failure carries one entry per offending field — `{ field, constraints }`, where `field` is a dotted path from the request-body root (`location.city`, `owners.0.name`) and `constraints` are `class-validator` keys such as `isEmail` or `whitelistValidation`. Constraint keys are deliberately machine-readable and carry no message text: a client maps them to its own localised copy, and nothing quoting a DTO message or a received value crosses the wire. Sent identically in every environment (#110) — unlike other error text, this is not affected by `disableErrorMessages`. Other errors may carry a single descriptive string, or an array of strings. Always sent — an error with no extra context carries an empty array.
